What the Archive Is For

Keeping things is not the same as hoarding them.

Ada Quill
Apr 2, 2026

My grandmother kept every letter she was ever sent, in shoeboxes, in the order they arrived. She could not have found any one of them in under an afternoon. It was a collection, and a lovely one, but it was not an archive.

An archive is a collection you can ask questions of. The difference is retrieval: whether the thing you kept comes back when you need it, from the scrap of it you still remember. Scholars used to manage this with marginalia and index cards, which is to say with a great deal of patience.

Most of what we save from the web lands in the shoebox. Bookmarks folders, open tabs, a reading list that only ever grows. We keep the address and trust that the page, and our memory of why it mattered, will both still be there.

Neither usually is. So before the practical part of this piece, one rule, which is the whole argument in miniature: keep the words and not just the link.
